solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: After second day out, David's back in bed

definitions.text: After second day out, David's back in bed

parts.words: After second day out, David's back in bed
parts.note: with the second D (day) taken out, DAVID becomes DAVI; read back it is IVAD, which spells out IV (Roman four) and AD (a poster), and the clue ends on what that pair names, a bed

explanation.surface: Someone back from a day trip, David is once more tucked up in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds IVAD, not the answer's letters: IV is four in Roman numerals and an AD is a poster, so IVAD is a coded picture of the answer, with 'bed' its definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional bed with a tall post at each corner, often hung with curtains.

clue.text: Supporting retirement of unfinished clue?

indicators.note: of here means made up of, the bed having the shortened clue word lying inside it

parts.note: going to bed is retiring for the night, so retirement is BED

indicators.note: unfinished says the final letter of the clue word is cut off

parts.note: a clue is a HINT

explanation.surface: A crossword question about backing for withdrawing an incomplete clue.
explanation.walkthrough: No indicator signals the insertion: 'retirement of' the clipped clue is read as the bed holding it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be right there backing someone up is to stand in their corner; the word is used for giving support.

clue.text: Irish nationalist sect, with name changed

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of the two words are put into a different order

explanation.surface: A splinter group of Irish nationalists rebrands itself under a new name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Roger Casement was an Irish nationalist executed for treason in 1916 after seeking German aid for the Easter Rising.

clue.text: A little Italian flower firm

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Po is Italy's longest river
CO is the usual abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A small Italian flower-selling business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a river here, one that flows; 'Italian' does double duty, pointing at the Po too.
explanation.definitionFit: Poco is the Italian word, used as a musical direction, meaning a little or slightly.

clue.text: Roughly deflower a lass? No fool, but arguably a horny beast

indicators.note: roughly says the letters are handled loosely and come out in a new order
No asks for the following word's letters to be absent from the phrase before

parts.note: an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A crude seduction attempt by a lecherous man who, though no fool, is called a randy animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No fool' removes ASS from A LASS, leaving AL; 'Roughly' scrambles DEFLOWER with AL. 'Arguably' covers the fact that deer carry antlers rather than true horns.
explanation.definitionFit: A fallow deer is a European species with broad palmate antlers, loosely called horns.

clue.text: Work as Nato manager?

indicators.note: a manager is one who handles or arranges things, so the preceding letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: Doing a job as an administrator for the Atlantic alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manager' is an unusual signal: the letters of AS NATO are managed into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonata is a musical composition, and a piece of music is a work.

clue.text: Port in a combination of single, double and treble

definitions.meaning: a major seaport city in China

definitions.text: a combination of single, double and treble
definitions.meaning: in darts, hitting the single, double and treble of one number with the three darts of a turn

explanation.surface: A harbour town found in a mix of three drinks of different sizes.
explanation.walkthrough: Single, double and treble sound like measures at a bar, but they are darts scoring segments.
explanation.definitionFit: Shanghai is China's great seaport, and the darts term names that three-dart feat.

clue.text: Flower girl having one-night stands, reportedly

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: in a down clue, stands means the letters are set upright, read from the bottom
reportedly tells us night is taken as it is heard, as the title-holder knight

parts.note: night is heard as knight, and a knight is addressed as SIR

explanation.surface: A girl with a habit of casual flings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one-night stands' seems a single phrase, but splits into one (I), night (heard as knight, SIR) and stands (turned upward). 'reportedly' marks the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris is a garden plant with showy blooms; the word is also a girl's name.

clue.text: Somehow it's right, following A-road to Heanor after accident

indicators.note: following says the single letter for right comes after everything else

parts.note: A read as one and road as way

indicators.note: after an accident things are in disarray, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Directions to Heanor, a Derbyshire town, after a crash: it is right, on the A-road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A-road' looks like a highway designation but splits into A (one) and road (way). Heanor is a small town in Derbyshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Both expressions mean by some means or other, without saying which method.

clue.text: Essentially Micra is easy to jack up

indicators.note: essentially here means at the core, so the letters are found in the middle of the run of words

explanation.surface: A small Nissan car is simple to lift on a jack.
explanation.walkthrough: The Micra is a small Nissan hatchback.
explanation.definitionFit: To jack something up is to lift or elevate it, whether a car or a price.

clue.text: What some artists use as representation of a lion and its pride, primarily

indicators.note: a representation is a depiction, and here the letters are rendered in a fresh arrangement
primarily picks only the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Painters depicting a lion and its family group, the pride.
explanation.definitionFit: Paints made with pigment in a drying oil are a classic medium for painters on canvas.

clue.text: Rum guy, member of secret society

parts.note: rum is old slang for strange, odd
a guy is a man, a fellow

explanation.surface: A strange man belongs to a clandestine organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum is old British slang for strange, not the spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oddfellows are a fraternal order with secret rituals; a member is one of them.

clue.text: Can 1960s film contain terrifyingly destructive goddess doubles?

indicators.note: contain says the outer letters hold the following ones within them

parts.note: can is slang for a toilet, a loo
Kes is Ken Loach's 1969 film about a boy and his kestrel
Kali is the Hindu goddess of time and destruction

explanation.surface: Asks whether a sixties movie could feature body doubles of a fearsome goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' opens as a question but is a noun meaning a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: People who closely resemble others are doubles, as in a star's stand-in.

clue.text: Short program with concealed bug

indicators.note: short asks for the word to be cut by its last letter

parts.note: an app is a computer program
concealed means hid

explanation.surface: A brief piece of software contains a hidden bug, as in a coding error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' suggests software or a listening device but means an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenfly and blackfly are sap-sucking insects, and an insect is a bug.

clue.text: Reduce intensity of drama's opening, having drunk ale with cast

parts.note: the first letter of drama is D, spelt out as DEE

indicators.note: drunk means the letters are reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: A play's first night calms down once the cast has been drinking beer.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letter D is given as its spoken name, DEE.
explanation.definitionFit: To calm a conflict or crisis is to make it less severe, scaling it down.

clue.text: One with testing work, reassembling electronic motorbike part?

indicators.note: reassembling means putting the pieces together in a new order

explanation.surface: A mechanic with a demanding job is rebuilding a part from an electric motorbike.
explanation.definitionFit: Small motorcycles are often powered by a motor firing once every two piston movements.

clue.text: Frank has to get rid of old-fashioned heater

parts.note: frank means candid, open
to get rid of an employee is to fire them

explanation.surface: Frank is told to dispose of an outdated heating appliance.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a man's name but means candid.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearth with burning coal or logs was the traditional way to warm a room.

clue.text: Aristocrat upset good French lover

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the word bottom to top

parts.note: bon is French for good
leman is an archaic word for a lover or sweetheart

explanation.surface: A peer is distressed by a fine French paramour.
explanation.definitionFit: A titled member of the peerage, such as a lord or duke, is a man of noble rank.

clue.text: Female flyer about to meet first lady

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Eve was the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: A woman pilot is about to be introduced to the President's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First lady' suggests the President's spouse but means Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruff is a wading bird; its female has a distinct name in birdwatching.

clue.text: Not easily excited, supporting the Spanish team

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting puts this piece beneath the next

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
an even temper is calm and steady

explanation.surface: A calm fan backing the side from Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket side fields this many players, so the number names the team.

clue.text: Take a little time getting into a clinch, oddly, as a circus act?

indicators.note: getting into means these letters go inside the others
oddly picks the first, third and fifth letters

parts.note: to rob is to take
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Taking a moment to embrace someone, asking whether this is a circus act.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'a' goes in with ROB and T; the second stands before the odd letters of clinch.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumbling and trapeze work in the ring is the stuff of a gymnastic, agile performer.

clue.text: Excellent clue, including helpful abbreviation for the reader

indicators.note: including means the first word's letters hold the next

parts.note: a tip is a clue or hint
PTO, please turn over, tells a reader to turn the page

explanation.surface: Praise for a fine clue containing a useful note for the solver.
explanation.definitionFit: Something first-rate or of the highest quality is described with this informal term.

clue.text: If so, could be no number nine playing with Gulf State's right winger

definitions.text: If so, could be no number

indicators.note: playing means the letters are toyed with into a new order
the right wing is the far end, so the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A football centre-forward lining up beside a right winger from a Gulf country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is not a figure but more numb; someone without feeling could be no number. 'number nine' and 'right winger' borrow football positions.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking sensation or sympathy cannot become more numb, the joke's premise.

clue.text: As far as possible, starting out afresh

indicators.note: afresh means the letters are dealt anew in another order
starting picks the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Going as far as one can, setting off all over again.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase marks a limit reached, as in walking until a certain point.

clue.text: Walk through part of airport, say

indicators.note: say means we hear the word rather than spell it

parts.note: passengers board at a gate in an airport

explanation.surface: Strolling through a section of an airport terminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's manner of walking, their stride or gait pattern, is a walk in that sense.

clue.text: Former footballer, throwing last boot out

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: throwing last means discarding the final letter

parts.note: Pele was the great Brazilian footballer

explanation.surface: A retired player discards his final football boot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boot' looks like footwear but 'boot out' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To eject or banish someone from a place or group is to kick them out.

clue.text: Work with skipper and his two best mates?

definitions.text: Work with skipper and his two best mates?

parts.words: Work with skipper and his two best mates
parts.note: a literary work about a boating trip by three friends, the 'skipper' a jokey nod to the boat and the dog

explanation.surface: Doing a job with a captain and his two closest friends.
explanation.walkthrough: Jerome K. Jerome's comic 1889 novel follows three friends rowing up the Thames with a dog, Montmorency.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of a Victorian comic novel about a trio's boating holiday on the Thames.
